## Proof placement

Claim: "270,000 hours of real-world manipulation data" - Proof on /blog/gen-0, in pretraining dataset section with specific phrase "pretrained on our in-house robotics dataset, which includes over 270,000 hours of real-world diverse manipulation data". Growth rate cited same section.

Claim: "growing at a rate of 10,000 hours a week and accelerating" - Same /blog/gen-0 section.

Claim: "Millions of robots are operating in the world today. Billions more are coming" - Homepage blog preview, full article at /blog/accelerating-the-next-phase-of-physical-ai. No external source cited.

Claim: "improves average success rates to 99% on tasks where previous models achieve 64%" - /blog/gen-1 with three specific task examples (vacuums, boxes, phones). No comparison dataset named.

Claim: "completes tasks roughly 3x faster than state of the art" - /blog/gen-1. Box folding 2.8x, phone packing 2.8x cited. No external benchmark source.

Claim: "GEN-1, our latest milestone...first general-purpose AI model that crosses a new performance threshold: mastery of simple physical tasks" - Homepage blog preview and /blog/gen-1. Mastery defined operationally by success rates, no external validation cited.

Claim: "over half a million hours of high-fidelity physical interaction data" - /blog/gen-1. No growth rate or collection scope detail provided here.

Claim: "trained from scratch — approximately 99% of the parameters from scratch" - /blog/beyond-world-models. Contrasts with fine-tuning but no performance comparison provided.

Non-proof claims: "building general intelligence for the physical world" (hero, /about) - aspirational, no evidence on site. "Robots can help us build more and get more done" (/about) - general statement, no evidence. Physical commonsense argument (/blog/physical-commonsense) - philosophical premise, no quantitative validation.

## Claim qualification

When claims lack proof: construct is assertion + implication without hedging. Example: "We train robots that work" (present tense, no qualification, no evidence structure). 

Unproven claims stay isolated in separate sections with minimal cross-linking. Example: Team credentials (/about) state "previously created" named models (PaLM-E, RT-2, Gemini Robotics) but do not link to papers or provide verifiable contribution details. Implicit authority transfer: credible past organizations (OpenAI, DeepMind, Boston Dynamics) listed without qualification.

Aspirational claims (AGI, general intelligence) appear only in positioning sections (/about, blog intro) not in data sections. When performance claims are made (/blog/gen-1), they include numeric specifics (99%, 1 hour, 2.8x) but no confidence intervals or test conditions.

Partnership claims mention "multiple data foundry partners" and "Partner & Customer-inspired applications" (/blog/gen-0, Table 1) with zero named entities or verifiable links.

## Conversion path

1. Entry: Homepage landing
2. Path A (Engagement): Click "Learn More" > /about > Read mission + team credentials > "Interested in working together?" > Choose Contact Us or Careers link
3. Path B (Information): Click "See all blog posts" > /blog > Select article > Read technical claims + performance data
4. Path C (Recruitment): Click Careers from nav or homepage CTA > /careers > View 18 open positions > Apply (external ATS assumed, not on-site form)
5. Path D (Partnership/Sales): Click Contact Us > /contact > Fill form (Name, Email, Phone, Company, Video/links describing automation need, Message) > Submit to info@generalistai.com

Contact form explicitly requests "If you have a particular use case for robots, please include links to videos of the tasks or processes you're interested in automating." This frames first conversation around specific automation scenarios, not generic inquiry.

Conversion metric: Contact form acts as first lead qualifier (company + use-case video). Careers page acts as recruitment funnel (18 roles + apply buttons).

## Distinctive

Tagline positioning: "Simplicity Scales" combined with "All videos 1x speed, fully autonomous" is distinctive. Claims themselves (the performance numbers) are common in AI, but the pairing of simplicity messaging + proof-via-video (no synthetic/sped-up footage) is specific. It positions the company on demonstration authenticity rather than architectural novelty. No competitor observed using this exact pairing in scout brief.

## Noise

Blog article "The Robots Build Now, Too" (Sept 2025) and "Research Preview" (June 2025) focus on niche tasks (Lego replication, sensorimotor control) without clear commercial connection to the broader "general intelligence" mission. These read as research hobby content rather than product-market fit evidence. The frequency and length of blog posts (8 articles in 12 months, some 12-14 min reads) suggests thought-leadership publication cadence, common in frontier AI but adds informational noise without driving conversion or proving claims.

## Not accessible

/research, /products, /company, /investors, /news - all return 404. No secondary navigation to deeper pages beyond Index, Blog, About, Careers, Contact. Blog article URLs follow predictable slug format (/blog/gen-0, /blog/gen-1, /blog/beyond-world-models); no archive pagination or search functionality observed in fetches. Contact form fields (Name, Email, Phone, Company, Video/links, Message) described from fetch response but form submission mechanics not tested. No JavaScript-gated content detected.
